uses.quote: Using gen AI tools without permission in your course work is academic misconduct.
List possible topic angles, generate questions to explore, and suggest themes or debates.
Brainstorm ideas and outlines to overcome writer's block.
Translate readings into different languages, making them easier to digest.
Create an audio version of notes or readings to review content.
Create study questions that promote deeper and more active learning strategies to move beyond memorization (see: Bloom's Taxonomy).
Create additional practice problems and explain solution logic for difficult content.
Identify grammar errors, generate synonyms, and polish sentence structure.
Generate search terms when doing online and library research.
Gen AI may be useful, but it can also be wrong. Before relying on any output, check the list below:
If you submit plagiarized work generated by a gen AI tool, you are responsible for the plagiarism, and it is considered academic misconduct.
Before using gen AI in your research and/or writing, talk with your advisor and supervisory committee.
uses.anchor: Graduate Student Research and Gen AI

default_when_silent.quote: If your instructor has not clearly stated that gen AI is permitted, assume it's not.

decided_by.quote: Before using gen AI in any course, always check your course outline and your instructor’s expectations.

duty.quote: Whenever you use gen AI, cite or acknowledge it.

contents.quote: I acknowledge the use of [insert AI system(s) and link] to [specific use of generative artificial intelligence]. The prompts used include [list of prompts].
